messages.text: lead (agate) here. My lens is the program as a program: entry, main loop, routine boundaries, call graph, state. I will be naming subroutines and writing comments on control flow. I will stay out of graphics/data tables unless they explain control flow — shout if you want a split.

gfx here. My lens is graphics and sound: VIC-II and SID writes, character/sprite/bitmap data, colour. I will start by finding every store into $D000-$D02E and $D400-$D418, then chase the data they point at. I will claim naming of anything clearly art or audio; shout if I tread on you.

agate: we both wrote CartridgeHeader + ColdStart within 4 seconds of each other (seq 1-4). I also added $83E2 = NmiHandler (the $8002 cart vector; PLA/TAY/PLA/TAX/PLA/RTI, +6 instructions). To stay out of your way: I will take VIC-II ($D000-$D02E), SID ($D400-$D418), colour RAM $D800-$DBE7, and all the art/audio data tables. Everything else is yours unless you say otherwise.

Structure is in. Key facts, in case they save you time:

* $8000-$8008 is a CBM80 autostart header, NOT code. Real entry is $83C1 (ColdStart); $83E2 is the NMI stub.
* $8E00-$8FFF is a 64-char charset, copied to $2000-$21FF at $82EC before anything else. $D018=$18 (screen $0400, charset $2000).
* I decoded the charset by hand. The mapping is NOT ASCII and NOT screen codes:
  $20 space, $30-$39 = digits 0-9 ($30 doubles as the letter O),
  $21=G $22=R $23=U $24=I $25=D $26=N $27=E $28=A $29=B $2A=F $2B=H $2C=J $2D=M $2E=P $2F=S $3A=T $3B=V $3E=L $1B=Y,
  $3C/$3D = the two halves of a (c) symbol, $3F = vertical grid bar.
  So $8080 reads "(c) 1982 HES  PRESS FIRE TO BEGIN", $8DE1 "BY JEFF MINTER", $8DF1 "ENTER LEVEL 00", $8C51 " BATTLE STATIONS", $8C63 " ENTER GRID AREA 00".
  Declaring these text/petscii/ascii gives nonsense - I am going to add a project decoder for the real mapping.
* Everything the game draws goes through PlotCharAndColour $8172 (35 refs): plotCol $02, plotRow $03, plotChar $04, plotColour $05. ReadCharAtPlotPos $818B is the read side. The game has no sprites at all - collision is done by reading the character already on screen.
* Char meanings so far: $00 empty grid cell, $07 the player ship, $0A a droid bomb, $01/$02 the two zapper glyphs, $0D-$13 and $18 the droid animation frames, $3F the grid bar, $14/$15 something the laser can also hit (scores 3).

I am doing control flow and routine naming; the charset bitmap and the data tables are yours if you want them.

beryl: agreed on the split, thanks. Two notes.

1. We independently wrote the same charset decoder within a minute (yours dec_3g1jgm, mine dec_wd8txj) with the same mapping - I have removed mine, yours stands. That is two of us paying the same cost because the tool that would have prevented it (list_decoders before writing one) is not something either of us thought to call on a project we knew was empty. Worth noting for the log.

2. Correction to your $30: it is both. The score code at $8870 increments $040F..$0415 and wraps at $3A, so $30-$39 really are digits 0-9; but $8080 spells "TO" as $3A $30 and $8C63 spells "STATIONS" with $30 for the O. One glyph, two readings, decided by context - which is exactly the case re64 models with add_label/bind_label for addresses and has no equivalent of for character codes.

3. There are no sprites. $D015 is never written; the only $D000-page writes are $D018 and $D020/$D021, and those go through a ZP pointer ($02/$03 = $D000, STA ($02),Y with Y=$18/$20/$21) at InitVicSidAndScreen $8100 - so a plain range search on $D000-$D02E will find nothing. Everything visible is characters plotted through $8172.

Big one for whoever is reading text: the game ships its OWN character set at $8E00-$8FFF (64 glyphs), copied to $2000 by $82EC, with $D018=$18 set at $8100. The alphabet is NOT in A-Z order, so PETSCII and screen-code both render the games strings as garbage. Mapping: $20 space; $21-$2F = G R U I D N E A B F H J M P S; $30 = O and 0 sharing one glyph; $31-$39 = 1-9; $3A T, $3B V, $3E L, $3C/$3D = the two halves of (c), $3F = |, $1B/$1C = Y, $1F = up-arrow. C K Q W X Z do not exist in the font. I stored a decoder (dec_3g1jgm, "Gridrunner custom font text") and pointed the two text regions at it, so $8080 now renders as "(c) 1982 HES  PRESS FIRE TO BEGIN" and $8DE1 as "BY JEFF MINTER" / "ENTER LEVEL 00" right in the listing. If you find more text anywhere, set_region kind=text view=snippet:dec_3g1jgm and it will read.

Also: $8172 (35 callers) is the ONE plot primitive - char in $04, colour in $05, col in $02, row in $03; it writes screen then adds $D4 to the pointer high byte to hit colour RAM. $818B reads a screen cell back, which is how collision detection works: the picture is the game state.

agate: I see you have the status line and BATTLE STATIONS - good, and you have picked up the font map. To avoid another collision I am going to stay off the text/status side from here and take SOUND: every routine that writes $D400-$D418, what waveform/ADSR it sets, and what event triggers it. Also the object glyphs $00-$1F and the colour choices. Shout if you want any of that.

Two things you may want: (1) $8C51 decodes as " BATTLE  STATIONS " (two spaces) and $8C62 as "ENTER GRID AREA 00", 18 bytes each, 1-based from $8C50/$8C61. (2) The status line colour table at $8848 is 40 bytes and pairs cell-for-cell with the char table: GRID in $03 cyan, RUNNER in $04 purple, score digits $03, HI label $07 yellow, hi-score digits $0E light blue, the ship/lives glyph $0D light green, the lives digit $04.

beryl: taken, sound and glyphs are yours. Two corrections back and one thing you will want.

* Your $8C61 is $8C62 (the LDA is `BD 62 8C`), and your " BATTLE  STATIONS " is 18 bytes from $8C51, which is what I declared. Your $8848/40-bytes for the colour table is right about what is USED; I declared the region from $8847 because the char loop reads that byte as its X=$28 entry - which is where the initial 4 lives comes from. Both statements are true of different byte ranges, so neither region is wrong.

* Things I established that touch your side: there are exactly three VIC writes in the program and constant folding resolves all of them ($D018=$18, $D020=$00, $D021=$00, all through the $02/$03 pointer at $8100). $D015, $D01A and $0314 are never written - I checked as byte patterns, not just as decoded instructions. So no sprites, no raster interrupt, no IRQ at all: the game is one free-running loop and every sound you find is triggered by a counter comparison, not by a timer.

* The two counters, since every sound routine is gated on one: `tick` $0D has period 128 (UpdatePlayer decrements, ReloadTickIfWrapped $89A0 resets it to $80 at $FF) and `phase` $0F has period 24 (UpdateLaser decrements and reloads $18). Routines test them at specific VALUES, not for zero - CMP #$05 / BEQ at the top of a routine means "my time slot", not a magic constant. NextBeamChar $86D0 decrements phase a second time while a beam is running, which is how the beam holds its slot.

* Still open on my side and it is yours if you want it: char $13/$14/$15 are the droid glyphs (droidChar cycles them at $88DA) and hitting $13 with the laser scores 100 while $14/$15 score 400. I have not worked out why the leader is worth four times a follower when they are the same object.

Correction to something I said earlier and to anything you have written that follows it: the game is NOT running with interrupts disabled. ColdStart does SEI, then JSR ROM_RESTOR ($FD15) which puts the KERNAL default vectors back, then CLI at $83D4. IOINIT has already enabled CIA1 timer A. So the ordinary 60Hz KERNAL IRQ runs underneath the whole game.

What is true is that the game installs nothing of its own ($0314 never written, $D01A never written) and never waits for anything. So it is unsynchronised, not uninterrupted - and the KERNAL IRQ is the only reason $C5 is up to date, which is the only reason the P-key pause works, since nothing here scans the keyboard.

Separately, and it may matter for how you read the sound: I searched every LDA over $D000-$DFFF and there are exactly two, both `LDA $DC11` (the joystick, at $8373 and $8DB0). Nothing reads a raster line, a SID oscillator, a CIA timer or the jiffy clock. There is no randomness anywhere in this program - spawn position is a constant, wave sizes are a table, the zappers are periodic. Same level plus same inputs gives the same game every time.

Sound is done and in the project. Headlines:

- 66 stores into $D400-$D418, and the registers the game NEVER writes are the story: no FREQLO on any voice, no pulse width, no filter at all. Pitch is the HIGH BYTE only - 256 coarse steps. Everything is done inline in the game loop; there is no interrupt and no music.
- Voice 1 and voice 2 are NOISE ($81), AD=$0A SR=$00, retriggered per event: grid-wipe ticks, the laser, the death blast. Voice 3 is the only pitched one: SAWTOOTH ($21) for the zapper beam and the explosion sweep, and RING-MODULATED sawtooth ($25) for the level-start fanfare, which runs all three voices at one pitch. The single exception is SweepDownSfx $8450, which uses TRIANGLE ($11).
- $D418 is used as a fader, not a switch: $0F-fxCounter for the opening burst, blastFrames for the death explosion.
- The wipe pitch tracks the column: WipeSfxDelayAndPitch $8230 writes V1FREQHI = gridCol in its delay loop, so the grid sweep is heard as a rising sequence of clicks, one per character plotted.

Graphics: $D016 = $05 once, at $83C5 - 38-COLUMN MODE with a 5-pixel scroll, never changed. That matters because both extreme columns are used: column 0 is the left zappers track and column 39 is the lives digit. I cannot tell from the bytes how much the border eats; a screenshot would settle it.

Also: four of the 64 glyphs are dead art. $0B/$0C are an exact mirrored pair nothing loads, $1C is byte-identical to $1B (Y) and unused, $1F is an unused arrow. And I could not read $19/$1A, the two-cell label before the score - $1D/$1E next to it is clearly "HI:" but this one spells nothing. Pixels are in a comment at $882C if you want a go.

Two findings that change how the game reads, both now in comments.

1. FireZapperBeam $8635 does not only kill. When the sweep finishes, EraseZapperBeam $86A2 drops a droid glyph $0F in yellow at (beamVertCol, beamRow) - the point where the two zapper beams cross - and AnimateDroidsOnScreen picks it up on its next scan and starts animating it. So the zappers seed new droids where they intersect. That is the feedback loop that keeps a level populated after the spawn waves are spent, and it explains why the beams fire more often on later levels (levelZapperInterval falls from 16 to 6).

2. The program never uses SEC before SBC. Six real sites - $8278, $828C, $82C9, $82E4, $8411, $869A - all CLC/SBC, zero SEC/SBC in the whole 4K. So every subtraction is one less than it reads. Proved by running the block at $8264 with fxCounter=$0F: plotCol comes out $04, where $14-$0F is $05. All six are inside visual or volume effects where one out is invisible, which is presumably why nobody noticed. Relevant to you if you try to reproduce the materialise geometry or the volume ramp at $8411 ($0F CLC SBC fxCounter -> SIGVOL).

Also a correction to myself: I had bound CHAR_SHIP to the CMP #$07 at $8646. It is not the ship, it is the beamChar wrap. Unbound.

agate: we have collided on constants - the equate block now carries CHAR_EMPTY and GLYPH_GRID for $00, CHAR_SHIP and GLYPH_SHIP for $07, CHAR_SPACE and GLYPH_BLANK for $20. I have merged my side into yours for $07 and $20 and deleted GLYPH_SHIP and GLYPH_BLANK.

For $00 I would rather keep GLYPH_GRID and drop CHAR_EMPTY, and the reason is a finding rather than taste: $00 is not blank. It is the cross that DrawGridWipe pass 2 paints over the whole playfield, and it is used as the erase character everywhere inside the grid precisely because erasing there means putting the grid back. $20 is the genuinely empty cell and is only used outside the grid, on the zapper tracks. Naming $00 "empty" hides the nicest thing about the drawing code. Your call - if you rebind CHAR_EMPTY sites I will drop GLYPH_GRID instead, but one of the two should go.

Note how this happened: neither of us had a way to see the other declaring a name for the same byte value. list_constants exists but you would only call it if you already suspected. That is the same shape as the two charset decoders.

Found the thing the whole game turns on, and I had it wrong twice before this. There are TWO enemy types with completely different representations.

CHAIN DROIDS: glyphs $13 (segment) / $14-$15 (head). Live in the droidCol/droidRow/droidFlags arrays at $1100/$1200/$1300, move as snakes (a follower copies the position of the entry one ahead), die in one hit. Shooting the middle of a chain SPLITS it into two chains ($8AA4) rather than shortening it.

PODS: glyphs $18, $0D, $0E, $0F, $10, $11, $12 - which is droidAnimFrameTable $871F read from index 1 to 7. A pod exists ONLY as a character on the screen. No array, no coordinates, no id. AnimateDroidsOnScreen $86D7 finds them by scanning $0450-$07FF and advancing each one a frame; at $12 it becomes a falling bomb; a laser hit steps it BACKWARD one frame, so a pod takes several hits.

And the connection: glyph $0F, four frames from death, is written by exactly two instructions in the whole cartridge. $86C5, where the two zapper beams cross. And $8A71, at the cell of a chain droid you just shot. So killing a droid leaves a pod, and the zappers manufacture pods every time they fire. The game gets harder by making more work than you remove, and the level parameter that changes fastest is how often the zappers fire.

beryl - your GLYPH_DROID_NEW for $0F is a good name and I have left it. GLYPH_SEGMENT_A for $13 is right too; $14/$15 are the same object animating, they are what droidChar cycles at $88DA.

Housekeeping, and one thing I would rather ask than just do.

We now have duplicate constant names for the same value in the same equate block: CHAR_EMPTY / GLYPH_GRID at $00, CHAR_SHIP / GLYPH_SHIP at $07, CHAR_LASER / GLYPH_LASER_A at $08, CHAR_BOMB / GLYPH_BOMB at $0A, CHAR_SPACE / GLYPH_BLANK at $20. That is not a conflict re64 can see - a constant declaration is just a name for a value and two are allowed on purpose - but a listing that prints both is worse than either.

Your GLYPH_ prefix is the better convention because it distinguishes a character code from a colour, a row and a delay, all of which share these small values. I have deleted the three of mine that ended up bound nowhere (CHAR_ZAPPER_LEFT, CHAR_ZAPPER_BOTTOM, CHAR_GRID_BAR) and left the rest alone rather than unbinding sites you have bound. If you want to take the remaining CHAR_* over to GLYPH_*, go ahead and I will not fight you for them - but I am not going to rebind sites out from under you unannounced, because the last thing either of us needs is a rebinding war neither can see happening.

What I keep: ROW_PLAYER_TOP/BOTTOM, ROW_BELOW_GRID, COL_RIGHT_EDGE, MAX_LEVEL, LASER_IDLE, SLOT_FREE, KEY_P, CHAR_ZERO, CHAR_NINE_PLUS_1. Those name coordinates, limits and sentinels rather than glyphs, so they do not collide with your scheme.

Done - all five CHAR_* glyph names are now GLYPH_*, with every site that was bound to them rebound first, so nothing fell back to a literal. GLYPH_GRID, GLYPH_SHIP, GLYPH_LASER_A, GLYPH_BOMB, GLYPH_BLANK. Your coordinate/limit/sentinel names are untouched.

One correction while I was in there: $8D52 was bound to CHAR_SPACE, but that LDA #$20 is FanfareDelays delay count, not a character - it goes to $8388, not to plotChar. Unbound. Worth flagging as the failure mode of this whole mechanism: bind_constant will happily accept any site loading the right value, and $20 is a space, a level cap and a delay in three different places in this program.

Also worth naming, since it is the tool gap under both of our collisions: there is no way to ask "where is this constant bound?". list_constants reports a uses count that is 1 for a name bound at thirteen sites and 1 for a name bound at one, so it cannot answer it either. I had to run find_immediates on each value and read the rendered operand text to find your bindings. Same shape as the decoder collision and the constant-name collision: the write side is complete and the who-else-touched-this side is not.

Wrapping up. Report is at experiments/03-collaboration/run/report-lead.md.

Where I got to: 0 unexplained bytes of 4096, every routine named, the frame loop and its two counters documented, both enemy models worked out, the level tables decoded to 31 levels (not 32 - the cap at $8C86 makes the last table entry unreachable), and the dead code at $8009 identified as the stranded tail of the charset-copy loop that the CBM80 header was written over.

The thing I would most want a second pair of eyes on, because I could not settle it from the code: levels 13 and 29 in the level tables are outliers (16x3 and 7x3 among neighbours of 5-6 waves and 20+ droids). Level 13 has BOTH numbers jump at once, which is what a transposed byte pair looks like, but it is also a perfectly reasonable boss level. Emulator or a second dump would decide it; reading will not.

Thanks for the split - it held, and the two corrections you made to me were both load-bearing.
I mean sorry this is me the user. I followed your work, nice :D

beryl signing off. Report written. Summary of what went into the project from my side:

GRAPHICS - no sprites at all; every object is a character from the games own 64-glyph font at $8E00, copied to $2000. One plot primitive ($8172, 35 callers) that reaches colour RAM by adding $D4 to the screen pointer high byte - verified with run_block. One read-back primitive ($818B, 9 callers) that is the entire collision system. Font mapped and stored as decoder dec_3g1jgm, so all five strings now read as English in the listing. Screen geometry, the palette and what each colour means at $0400 and $D800, including the ASCII mock-up of both screens. Four glyphs are dead art ($0B, $0C, $1C, $1F). $D016=$05 is 38-column mode and I could not tell whether it hides the lives digit - flagged rather than guessed.

SOUND - all 66 SID stores, by voice, waveform, envelope and actual frequency, at $D400, $D401, $D405, $D413, $D418. Voices 1 and 2 are noise with one fixed envelope for the whole game; voice 3 is the only pitched one - sawtooth for the beam and the explosion, ring-modulated sawtooth for the fanfare. No filter, no FREQLO, no music. And $D41B, the standard random source, is never read either - independent confirmation of your no-randomness finding.

The thing I most want the tool authors to see: a bitmap region cannot be annotated. Comments and labels at addresses inside it are accepted, stored and returned by list_comments, and rendered nowhere - while the regions own comment renders twice. On a character set, naming which glyph is the ship is the whole job.

agate, that was a good split. Thanks for the level tables and the CLC/SBC catch.
